review_notes: Read the whole file and checked Mathlib for HasFPowerSeriesAt.add/sub/neg, dslope_sub_smul(_of_ne), dslope_const (not present). Other proofs (dslope_sub_mul, sub_pow_mul, exists_taylor_remainder, congr) looked reasonably direct; I found no clear readable simplification there. Replacements are untested; the sub proof's rw step may need a `show`/`change` for the `f - g` vs lambda form.

findings.excerpt: have hneg : AnalyticAt ℂ (fun z => -g z) z₀ := by fun_prop
findings.problem: Subtraction is derived by a roundabout route: build analyticity of `-g`, apply the add lemma, rewrite with `taylorCoeffAt_neg`, prove a function equality by `funext; ring`, then rewrite with `sub_eq_add_neg`. The sibling `taylorCoeffAt_add` instead goes directly through the power-series bridge, and Mathlib has `HasFPowerSeriesAt.sub`, so the same short argument works for subtraction.
findings.proposed_change:
Mirror `taylorCoeffAt_add`:
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hf
  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := hg
  have h := HasFPowerSeriesAt.taylorCoeffAt_eq (hp.sub hq) j
  rw [HasFPowerSeriesAt.taylorCoeffAt_eq hp j, HasFPowerSeriesAt.taylorCoeffAt_eq hq j] 
  exact h  -- the function `f - g` is defeq to `fun z => f z - g z`, and `(p - q).coeff j = p.coeff j - q.coeff j` by `rfl`
(possibly `show taylorCoeffAt (f - g) z₀ j = _` first, then `rw [taylorCoeffAt_eq (hp.sub hq) j, ...]; rfl`). This removes the `hneg`, `h1`, `h2` bookkeeping and `taylorCoeffAt_neg` dependency.
findings.benefit: Shorter proof with one uniform idea (reduce to power-series coefficients) shared with `taylorCoeffAt_add`; no auxiliary negation lemma or ring-based function equality needed.

findings.excerpt: have hstep : (fun z => ∑ i ∈ insert a s, G i z)
findings.problem: The inductive step proves a separate `hstep` function equality by `funext; rw [Finset.sum_insert ha]` just to rewrite the sum under the lambda binder, then rewrites again with `Finset.sum_insert ha` on the right-hand side.
findings.proposed_change: Replace `hstep` and the first two rewrites with `simp only [Finset.sum_insert ha]` (which rewrites under the binder and on the RHS), then `rw [taylorCoeffAt_fun_add (hG a (Finset.mem_insert_self a s)) (Finset.analyticAt_fun_sum s fun i hi => hG i (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hi)), ih fun i hi => hG i (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hi)]`.
findings.benefit: Drops a 3-line auxiliary equality; the step reads as 'split off the head term, use additivity, apply induction hypothesis'.
